open_points.subject: agent submission of personal-data values
open_points.text: State 0 says "the owner alone reads" personal data and A07 concludes that "no agent ever holds it", but agents may start runs, compose constants and author trial cases whose requests contain the actual values; no rule refuses an agent-supplied `personal_data` value.
open_points.question: Is the personal-data guarantee only about values returned by the kernel, or must requests from agents containing plaintext `personal_data` be refused?
options: The guarantee is outbound only; agents may submit plaintext personal data
Refuse plaintext personal data in every agent request
Permit it only for specified actions or sources
open_points.default_guess: Treat the guarantee as outbound only, because A07's normative rule is phrased as what the surface returns.

open_points.subject: A07 execution class
open_points.text: Rule 5 defines an execution's class as "the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs" but gives no result when the execution names no inputs and, for an operation, no outputs.
open_points.question: What disclosure class does an inputless execution have for purposes such as redacting its `failure_detail`?
options: `open`
Use the node's proof-time output class
Execution class is absent until at least one value exists
open_points.default_guess: Use `open`, matching the rule for an inputless function's output.

open_points.subject: A07 failure-detail redaction
open_points.text: Rule 5 says a protected `failure_detail` is returned to an agent "only as its length and that class" without defining whether length means Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes, or the original pre-truncation length.
open_points.question: Which length is disclosed for a non-open `failure_detail`?
options: UTF-8 byte length of the stored bounded detail
Unicode scalar count of the stored detail
Original response or exception text length before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Return the UTF-8 byte length of the stored, already bounded detail.

open_points.subject: A07 approval-preview redaction
open_points.text: Rule 4 first says personal-data values in approval previews become digest and class, then says an agent gets "no built request for a preview any of whose inputs is `personal_data` — only the request's digest."
open_points.question: When any input is personal, does "only" replace just the built-request representation, or the entire preview including operation metadata and non-personal inputs?
options: Replace only the built request; retain operation metadata and separately redacted inputs
Return only `request_digest` and no other preview fields
Return operation metadata plus `request_digest`, but no input list
open_points.default_guess: Replace only the built request and retain the other preview fields under the ordinary value-redaction rules.

open_points.subject: mapped file-list disclosure
open_points.text: A13 says a mapped file list takes the highest class among its elements and that each reference naming an element carries the list's class, while M22 also gives each SpooledFile its own element class; A07 only specifies what happens to "a `personal_data` file" and defines no digest for a file list.
open_points.question: When a mapped file list is `personal_data` because only some elements are personal, what exactly may an agent see for the list and its open elements?
options: Apply the aggregate list class to every element and return each element only as digest and class
Redact each element according to its own SpooledFile class
Return one aggregate list digest and class
open_points.default_guess: Apply the aggregate class to every element reference and expose only each element's content digest and the aggregate class.

open_points.subject: service-returned credential data
open_points.text: State 0 says secrets "never enter ... an answer", but A17 rule 2 says a service response carrying a credential in another encoding "is not recognised, and is protected only by its class," allowing it to be used and returned.
open_points.question: Must all representations of a credential be excluded from answers, or is the State 0 promise limited to values the kernel inserts and verbatim echoes it can recognize?
options: The promise is limited to kernel-inserted values and recognized verbatim echoes
No credential representation may be returned, requiring broader detection
Encoded values may be stored but never returned
open_points.default_guess: Apply A17's narrower interpretation: reject only verbatim echoes and protect unrecognized encodings solely by disclosure class.

open_points.subject: credential header value
open_points.text: A17 accepts any nonempty UTF-8 credential value without a control character, while A09 requires that value to be sent verbatim as an HTTP header; neither text defines the allowed non-ASCII characters or their wire encoding.
open_points.question: Which credential characters are valid, and how is a valid non-ASCII value serialized into an HTTP header?
options: Require visible ASCII only
Allow ISO-8859-1 bytes
Allow UTF-8 header bytes
Use the HTTP client's header-value rules and treat rejection as `credential_unresolved`
open_points.default_guess: Require visible ASCII plus permitted horizontal space, rejecting anything the HTTP field-value grammar cannot represent unambiguously.

open_points.subject: credential control characters
open_points.text: A17 refuses a credential that "holds ... a control character" but does not define the character set covered by that term.
open_points.question: Does `control character` mean ASCII C0 plus DEL, Unicode general category `Cc`, C0/C1 controls, or another closed set?
options: ASCII C0 and DEL
Unicode category `Cc`
ASCII C0, DEL and C1 controls
open_points.default_guess: Reject Unicode category `Cc`, including C0, DEL and C1 control characters.

open_points.subject: selected instance name
open_points.text: M28 says an instance is selected "by its manifest instance name", while A17 only limits selection to at most one and does not say what happens at startup if the configured name is absent from the manifest.
open_points.question: Does an absent selected instance name prevent startup, count as no selected instance, or remain a selection whose requests fail for a missing address?
options: Refuse startup
Treat the service as having no selected instance
Start and fail that service's proposals and sends as address missing
open_points.default_guess: Start and treat the selected instance as unavailable, causing binding proposal or acceptance to fail and sends to report the applicable instance check.

open_points.subject: configuration security on token-list re-read
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration path to be opened without following symlinks and the file to be regular, owner-owned and private, but A16 says a live re-read applies "exactly four checks" and that every other start check applies only at restart.
open_points.question: When the token list is re-read after startup, are A17's no-symlink, ownership, regular-file and permission checks repeated?
options: Repeat every A17 secure-open and file-property check
Use no-follow opening but repeat only A16's four content checks
Perform an ordinary read and repeat only A16's four checks
open_points.default_guess: Use no-follow opening on every read, but treat changed ownership or mode as a restart-only check because A16 explicitly limits live validation to four checks.

open_points.subject: credential-header collision startup check
open_points.text: A09 says a credential header colliding with a required or kernel-set header "refuses to start", but no rule says what startup does when the selected instance or its manifest record is absent, malformed or unreadable while attempting that collision check.
open_points.question: How is the required startup collision check performed when the manifest cannot yield a valid selected instance?
options: Refuse startup because collision safety cannot be checked
Skip the collision check and defer manifest failure to proposal or send
Check only services whose selected instance can be read successfully
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup only for a collision found in a readable selected instance; defer absent or malformed manifest data to binding and invocation checks.

open_points.subject: A17 startup-check precedence
open_points.text: A17 and A09 define several startup refusals—configuration file type, ownership, permissions and symlinks; credential header syntax and absolute paths; and header collisions—but give no order for choosing the reported failure when several hold.
open_points.question: In what fixed order are A17-related startup checks performed and which failure is reported first?
options: Configuration path security, parse/schema, credential declarations, then manifest header collisions
Parse/schema first, then file security, then credential and manifest checks
Report all startup failures together
open_points.default_guess: Check configuration path security first, then parse and field validity, then credential declarations, then manifest-dependent header collisions.

open_points.subject: mapped element retry eligibility
open_points.text: A13 rule 2 says a mapped pass runs elements with "no concluded record" and that "a concluded element is never executed again", but `service_unreachable` and `outcome_unknown` attempts write NodeExecution records and A11/A14 require later attempts for those same elements.
open_points.question: Which NodeExecution statuses make a mapped element terminal, and which merely conclude an attempt while leaving the element eligible for another attempt?
options: Only successful, failed, skipped and upstream-failed element conclusions are terminal; waiting statuses remain retryable
Any NodeExecution is terminal, requiring retries to be represented outside mapped execution
The latest waiting record is replaced rather than adding another NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Distinguish attempt conclusion from element conclusion: `service_unreachable` and unresolved or `not_applied` unknown outcomes remain eligible for a new numbered attempt.

open_points.subject: map_index numbering
open_points.text: Mapped elements are identified and ordered by `map_index`, but no text states whether the first element has index 0 or 1; only `list_index` is explicitly defined as starting from 0.
open_points.question: What `map_index` is assigned to the first mapped element?
open_points.default_guess: Use zero-based indexing, matching `list_index` and JSON list indexing.

open_points.subject: receiving-port validation timing
open_points.text: A13 says a value is validated against the target port "before it enters a node" and a violation immediately concludes the receiving node, while readiness requires every input port to hold its value and the resulting record names "the inputs it had."
open_points.question: Is target validation performed and recorded as each edge delivers, potentially before other inputs arrive, or only after all inputs are present and the node is selected?
options: Validate on delivery and fail immediately with the inputs available then
Validate all inputs only when the node becomes ready and is selected
Validate on delivery but defer the NodeExecution until all other inputs become settled
open_points.default_guess: Validate on delivery and conclude immediately, recording only inputs delivered by that point.

open_points.subject: failed function with multiple outputs
open_points.text: A13 says an unsuccessful element keeps no output but files written before most failures remain in the spool and count toward the run ceiling; it does not define the order in which multiple returned output ports and file-list elements are validated, spooled and published.
open_points.question: If one returned output is invalid and another is a valid file, is that file written and retained as unnamed spool data, and what fixed port and element order decides this?
options: Stage every returned output, then validate; retain all staged files on non-ceiling failure
Validate all values and types before writing any file
Process ports by name and file elements by list order, retaining only files reached before the failure
open_points.default_guess: Process output ports by Unicode code-point name and file elements in list order; files staged before a non-ceiling failure remain unnamed in the spool.

open_points.subject: mapped output behind a disabled guard
open_points.text: A13 rule 6 says only a mapped list "that is delivered" is measured against `stored_value_bytes_max`, but does not say whether an output whose only outgoing guarded edge is disabled counts as delivered before or after the guard decision.
open_points.question: Can an oversized mapped list fail the node when every edge that could carry that output is disabled by its guard?
options: No; a disabled edge means the list is not delivered or measured
Yes; producing the output for an edge counts as delivery even when its guard is disabled
Measure it only if another enabled edge or flow output consumes the same port
open_points.default_guess: Do not measure it unless at least one enabled edge or flow output actually consumes it.

open_points.subject: successful run with skipped output
open_points.text: M19 says a run is `succeeded` when "every node and output concluded successfully", while A13 expressly allows a flow output to be `skipped_by_guard` and still defines the run as succeeded when nodes are succeeded or skipped.
open_points.question: Does `skipped_by_guard` count as a successful conclusion for both nodes and flow outputs when determining the final run status?
options: Yes; skipped nodes and outputs are successful non-production
Skipped nodes are allowed but any skipped flow output prevents success
Use another final status when an output is skipped
open_points.default_guess: Treat `skipped_by_guard` as a successful non-production conclusion for both nodes and outputs, following A05 and A13.
